newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NICKLAUS KEEPS ROLLING AT MAJOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NICKLAUS KEEPS ROLLING AT MAJOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: After winning an unprecedented 18 major golf championships and playing in an incredible 41 consecutive U.S. Opens, Jack Nicklaus is a multi-millionaire with no more world's to conquer.
But at age 57, the Golden Bear says he's not ready to quit competing.
"I'm playing the best golf I've played in 10 years," he said after completing the U.S. Open at the Congresssional Country Club Sunday with a four-over-par 74 and a final total of 13 over par.
"I seem to be getting back into it. I'm healthier, my hip is working and I'm having fun," he added.
"I've enjoyed the years, and I've enjoyed the memories, and now I'd like to enjoy some more," he said.
He was cheered throughout the tournament by big galleries and enjoyed the fact that one of his fellow competitors was his son Gary.
Gary Nicklaus failed to make the cut, losing the chance to play the same Open as his dad on Father's Day. But another of Nicklaus's four sons, Jackie, was with him on the course Sunday as his caddie.
"He gave up his Father's Day for me. He has four kids at home and I really appreciate that," Nicklaus said.
Nicklaus left open the possibility that he would play in the British Open at Royal Troon in July, saying if he was playing well, he would add to his record by entering his 151st major championship.
